title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

errors: In the proof of (iii)⇒(ii) the hypothesis must be x ∥ F' (x disjoint from F'), not x ∥ F as written or transcribed. Otherwise the argument makes no sense.

In (ii)⇒(iii), concluding x ∥ F' from 'x is a cell of \overline{F'} not in F'' silently uses two things: that cells of a figure ≪ F are pairwise disjoint, and that x is irreducible (in 𝓛). These are presumably among the earlier axioms, but they are not cited.
Transitivity of ≪ (x ≪ \overline{F'} ≪ F ⇒ x ≪ F) is used without reference.
In (ii) of the corollary, 'x ∈ amb(X)' should evidently be 'x ∈ amb(F)' (or comb(F)), since there is no X in this statement.
The question whether (i)–(iii) imply the ≪-maximality (iv) is left open on this page.

ideas.what: Characterization of a subdivision/refinement F' ≼ F of a stratified figure by three equivalent conditions: a disjointness test, covering every stratum, and maximality among partial refinements.
ideas.modern_name: Refinement of stratifications / subdivision of cell complexes; axiomatic tame topology (o-minimal-style cell decompositions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology for subdivisions; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s); Grothendieck's call for 'topologie modérée' in the Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call for tame topology appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this axiomatic development is unpublished.

ideas.what: Existence axiom At 13 ('quasi-existence of elements' or 'completeness'): if some figure separates F from X, then a stratum of X already does.
ideas.modern_name: Separation/completeness axiom in an abstract lattice of tame sets (akin to atomicity/density conditions in lattice theory)

ideas.what: Locality of ≪ ('se prouve structure par structure', At 4) used to extend a partial refinement by adjoining a stratum.
ideas.modern_name: Locality of refinement; sheaf-like gluing of subdivisions

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether a subdivision (maximal for ≤ among ≪-minorants) is also maximal for the finer relation ≪. He leaves this open. It amounts to asking whether 'subdivision' is intrinsic to the ≪-order.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor foundational question within his unpublished axiomatics of tame topology. It could interest anyone trying to axiomatize o-minimal or definable cell structures order-theoretically, but it is a small point.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine lemma-proving inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs'. Characterizing subdivisions as maximal partial refinements is natural. The framework itself (an abstract tame topology as an order structure with existence axioms) is a mildly notable unpublished detail, but nothing on this page is a striking result.
transcription_corrections: Line 'si on a x ∈ ouvd F, avec x ∥ F': the reading 'ouvd' is doubtful. It is probably 'amb' or 'comb', and logically the condition should be x ∥ F'.
'car F' \not\leq \overline{F'}' should read 'car F' ≨ \overline{F'}' (strict inclusion), i.e. F' ≠ \overline{F'}.
'soit x ∈ \overline{F'} \setminus \widetilde{F'}' is closer to 'soit x ∈ \widetilde{\overline{F'}}, x ∉ \widetilde{F'}, x ∈ comb(X)', i.e. a cell of \overline{F'} that is not a cell of F'.
In (iii), 'Pour tout \overline{F'}' replaces a struck 'Il est maximal par ≪'. The crossed-out (iv) concerns maximality for ≪.
